text:
raj: Pushed a TF module PR: bump gpu_pool module to v3.0.0. Main goals: add region-aware spot fallback, make kms_alias optional, and change instance_type mapping to reduce cost. Need eyes on GitOps plan gating before we merge.

sasha: Can you paste the plan output? want to check provider alias changes and any IAM boundary edits.

raj: infra-bot ran plan in CI, attaching the cropped diff below. TL;DR: creates new google_compute_instance_template, updates module version, replaces kms key resource (alias optionalization), and a provider alias addition for asia-east1.

infra-bot: CI plan (summary): 
```
+ module.gpu_pool.module.instance_template.google_compute_instance_template.template[0]
~ module.gpu_pool.module.kms.google_kms_crypto_key.pool_key
+ provider.google.asia-east1 (new)
- resource.google_kms_crypto_key.kms_key (will be replaced)
```

lina: Replacing a KMS key is scary in prod. Did the PR include a migration path? rotating keys can break encrypted secrets for PVCs and kube secrets.

raj: I made kms_alias optional so we can stage without touching existing keys. But the plan shows replacement because default behavior in v3 flips `primary_region` handling. I added a migration script to copy key versions, but that script isn't automated in our GitOps flow.

pmartin: Suggest we gate any TF change that will replace a KMS resource. Add a policy in CI that marks the plan with the tag "kms-replace" and requires OWNER approval. We already have a policy for IAM role removals, extend it.

sasha: Also note provider alias additions can cause state split across workspaces if not carefully handled. We should ensure staged apply uses the same workspace and provider alias map before promoting.

raj: Proposed canary sequence:
1) Merge to main but hold the GitOps PR that applies to prod-argocd app.
2) Argo CD auto-sync to a dedicated canary cluster `gpupool-canary-us-west1` (labelled staging).
3) Run smoke tests: node registration, KV cache load, sample inference job, secret decrypt check.
4) If green, flip argocd to sync staging->prod subset via a selective patch that updates module version in prod-only overlay.

lina: Fine, but we need an automated smoke test for decrypt: try `kubectl get secret -n ml inference-creds -o yaml` and attempt a decrypt via kms-test utility. No manual steps.

pmartin: For the CI gating rule, here's a draft: if plan contains `replace.*google_kms_crypto_key` then fail PR unless label `kms-allow` and at least two OWNER approvals. Also post a deploy note to #incidents for tracking.

infra-bot: Note: plan-duration=avg 2m 10s across runs; adding provider setup for asia-east1 adds ~45s extra.

raj: Cost note: v3 maps smaller n1 -> n2-equivalent instance types with more VRAM per $ but higher baseline. Estimated monthly delta for our reserved pools: -12% token-cost per model but +8% infra bill. Worth it?

sasha: Seems OK if unit cost per token drops. We should run a 48h soak in canary with production-like QPS to verify throughput and memory OOM behavior.

pmartin: One more risk: GitOps auto-reconcile might detect module version drift and try to reapply across regions. We should add a plan hook that blocks reconciles if `module_version` changes without `gitops: true` flag in the overlay.

raj: Agree. I'll add a PlanCheck job in CI that: computes module lockfile diff, searches for `kms`/`provider.alias` changes, and sets a `plan-check:needs-approval` status on the PR.

lina: For the migration script: put it in ops/scripts/kms-migrate.sh and make it callable from a manual job in the GitHub Actions workflow. Document steps clearly: snapshot key versions, copy, rewrap, update annotations in k8s secrets, rotate consumers.

pmartin: Also add an audit tag to the TF change: `x-infra-change-id = "gpupool-v3-<pr-number>"` so we can correlate telemetry (cost, errors) after rollout.

raj: Will update PR with: CI policy rule, canary plan, smoke test steps, migration script path, and manual approval checklist. Planning to hold prod apply until onsign wheels-green.

oncall-bot: Reminder: if this touches provider aliases in asia-east1, ensure quota requests for GPUs are approved in that region before apply or the canary will fail.

sasha: Thanks. I'll review the PR later today. If everyone is aligned we can start staging canary tomorrow AM. :thumbsup:
